Kleiner Perkins is a profit seeking enterprise. They live or die based on their success. They need profit the way you need air or a plant needs sunlight. It would be economic suicide for the organization to discriminate against Ellen Pao or to fail to hire the most productive and talented employees available to them.

A business is run to amass profits. These profits don't care about gender, race, or any other superficial characteristics.

it’s absurd to conclude that gender discrimination is genuinely practiced in competitive industries. Any business who failed to obtain the best and brightest workers would be out-competed by other businesses who would not similarly fail. An all-white-male old boys club silicon valley firm, should one actually exist, would not long survive against it's more broadly staffed competitors who did not handicap themselves in a similar way.

Every private employer of course has the moral right, and should have the legal right, to hire and fire whomever it wants for whatever reasons might strike its fancy, as long as doing so does not violate a contractual agreement between the employer and employee.

But as an economic matter, any employer in a competitive industry who acts on prejudices that have no economic merit is an employer who is effectively removing all $20 bills from its wallet and throwing them on the ground, leaving these valuable assets available to be picked up and used productively – and against it – by its competitors. Any firm who hobbled itself in the marketplace and refused to accept $20 bills from the market would find such assets do not long lay unclaimed. They would find themselves at a fatal disadvantage quite quickly.

Ellen Pao’s suit is a perfect example of the feminist vendetta against Silicon Valley companies. That vendetta is based on the following conceit: Businesses refuse to hire or promote top-notch employees who would increase their profits, simply because those employees are female.

Reality check: Any employer who rejects talent out of irrational prejudice will be punished in the marketplace when competitors snap up that talent. For the feminist line of attack on Silicon Valley to be valid, every tech firm would need to be conspiring in an industry-wide economic suicide pact.

Kleiner Perkins had devoted considerable time and resources to developing Ms. Pao’s potential. The idea that the firm was simultaneously thwarting her because of her gender and forfeiting its own investment in her is absurd.

The market is the best antidote to discrimination. It rewards talent and penalizes prejudice. Silicon Valley has been an unprecedented cornucopia of life-transforming innovation. And a shining example of how entrepreneurial market forces increase society's wealth as a whole.

Kleiner Perkins might have won this recent skirmish, but Silicon Valley remains in the cross hairs of feminist crusaders and their media allies. Expect companies to load up on even more dead-weight bean-counting diversity officers and sexual-harassment trainers. The further this discriminatory charade expands, is the further we all become poorer and are deprived of the benefits of Silicon Valley inventiveness and creativity.
